SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. On most maps, which direction is at the top? (1 mark)
   A. South
   B. East
   C. West
   D. North

2. On a map of a village, the church is to the east of the school. On the map, where is the church drawn? (1 mark)
   A. Below the school
   B. Above the school
   C. On the left of the school
   D. On the right of the school

3. Which is the correct way to write the in-between point that is between south and west? (1 mark)
   A. South-west
   B. West-south
   C. Sowest
   D. West-south-west

4. Which county contains the capital city of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kisumu
   B. Kitui
   C. Nairobi
   D. Nakuru

5. Which of these uses the water of a river to make electricity? (1 mark)
   A. A church
   B. A market
   C. A hydroelectric power station
   D. A school

6. Which of these is most likely to happen in the rainy season? (1 mark)
   A. Herders move very far for water
   B. Grass dries up completely
   C. Rivers fill with water
   D. Farmers harvest all their maize

7. Which place in Nairobi shows traditional homes and dances of many communities? (1 mark)
   A. Lamu Old Town
   B. Gede Ruins
   C. Fort Jesus
   D. Bomas of Kenya

8. Who brings medicine and equipment to hospitals? (1 mark)
   A. Drivers and traders
   B. Nobody
   C. Only farmers
   D. Only teachers

9. Which artefacts are carved at Kisii and sold to visitors? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic toys
   B. Glass windows
   C. Iron bridges
   D. Soapstone carvings

10. What is a festival? (1 mark)
   A. A quiet day
   B. A river
   C. A big celebration
   D. A kind of house

11. Which statement about culture is true? (1 mark)
   A. Only one culture is right
   B. Culture is only about clothes
   C. Every community's culture deserves respect
   D. Culture never changes

12. Which is a traditional food eaten in many parts of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Ugali
   B. Sushi
   C. Hamburger
   D. Pizza

13. What is the history of a school? (1 mark)
   A. The school timetable
   B. The school bell
   C. The school menu
   D. The story of how it started and changed

14. Which of these is a jua kali product? (1 mark)
   A. A jet plane
   B. A big ship
   C. A metal door made in a small workshop
   D. A satellite

15. Which is not a good reason to choose a project? (1 mark)
   A. It is wanted
   B. We have the skills
   C. It is dangerous but exciting
   D. It is safe

16. A group spent Ksh 400 and earned Ksh 700. What is the profit? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 1,100
   B. Ksh 700
   C. Ksh 300
   D. Ksh 400

17. Which of these promotes peace? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Fighting
   C. Sharing
   D. Rumours

18. What is the Kiswahili word for peace? (1 mark)
   A. Chakula
   B. Rafiki
   C. Amani
   D. Shule

19. Which day is the International Day of Peace? (1 mark)
   A. 1 January
   B. 25 December
   C. 12 December
   D. 21 September

20. Why is it important to plan a peace-building activity? (1 mark)
   A. So that it wastes time
   B. So that nobody joins
   C. So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   D. So that it is cancelled

21. What is child labour? (1 mark)
   A. Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   B. Playing sports
   C. Doing homework
   D. Light help at home

22. Which day is celebrated on 16 June each year to honour children in Africa? (1 mark)
   A. Day of the African Child
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Jamhuri Day
   D. Labour Day

23. At what age can a person legally marry in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. 18 years
   B. 14 years
   C. 12 years
   D. 16 years

24. Which of these is a benefit of democracy in school? (1 mark)
   A. Only some pupils are heard
   B. Everyone has a voice
   C. Leaders are never checked
   D. Pupils are ignored

25. Who is a good resource person to learn about community leadership? (1 mark)
   A. A random shop
   B. A stranger who knows nothing
   C. A cartoon
   D. A village elder

26. Who leads a location and is appointed by the national government? (1 mark)
   A. Pastor
   B. Chief
   C. Clan elder
   D. Village poet

27. Which of these is a national government service? (1 mark)
   A. Cattle dips
   B. Pre-primary schools
   C. Defence and security
   D. County markets

28. Who approves the governor's choice of county executive committee members? (1 mark)
   A. The village elder
   B. The chief
   C. The teachers
   D. The county assembly

29. Who helps the governor? (1 mark)
   A. The driver
   B. The pupil
   C. The cook
   D. The deputy governor

30. What is devolution? (1 mark)
   A. Ending the government
   B. A kind of tax
   C. Keeping all power in one place
   D. Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain what harambee is and give one example of what it can be used for. (2 marks)

32. Explain how tourism can benefit a county and its people. (5 marks)

33. What is a county assembly? (2 marks)

34. What is a compass used for? (2 marks)

35. Give three school values and say why each is important. (3 marks)

36. Describe the steps in a fair class election. (4 marks)

37. State three duties of clan elders. (3 marks)

38. Explain why we say that the compass is useful in a county. (5 marks)

39. Describe how a class can invite a resource person to talk about leadership. (4 marks)

40. State three industries found in Kenya and the raw material each uses. (3 marks)

41. List the five items on the sample agenda for a Children's Government meeting. (5 marks)

42. Explain what devolution means. (2 marks)

43. Name four roles in a school enterprise team and state one duty for each. (4 marks)

44. A dot map has 1 dot for every 1,000 people. A town has 12 dots and a dry area has 2 dots. How many more people live in the town? Show your working. (3 marks)

45. Explain why children with special needs need extra care and respect. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — North
   Maps are drawn with north at the top unless a north arrow shows otherwise.

2. D — On the right of the school
   East is on the right when north is at the top.

3. A — South-west
   We say the north or south word first, so it is south-west.

4. C — Nairobi
   Nairobi County contains Kenya's capital city.

5. C — A hydroelectric power station
   Hydroelectric stations use falling river water to make electricity.

6. C — Rivers fill with water
   Rain fills rivers and streams.

7. D — Bomas of Kenya
   The Bomas of Kenya is a cultural centre in Nairobi.

8. A — Drivers and traders
   Transport workers carry goods to hospitals.

9. D — Soapstone carvings
   Kisii is known for soapstone carving.

10. C — A big celebration
   Festivals are big celebrations with songs and dances.

11. C — Every community's culture deserves respect
   We must respect all cultures.

12. A — Ugali
   Ugali is widely eaten in Kenya.

13. D — The story of how it started and changed
   History tells how the school began and grew.

14. C — A metal door made in a small workshop
   Jua kali workers make goods like doors and furniture.

15. C — It is dangerous but exciting
   A project must be safe for children.

16. C — Ksh 300
   700 - 400 = 300.

17. C — Sharing
   Sharing builds trust and friendship.

18. C — Amani
   Amani means peace.

19. D — 21 September
   The International Day of Peace is on 21 September.

20. C — So that it runs well and everyone knows what to do
   Planning helps activities succeed.

21. A — Hard or dangerous work that harms a child or stops schooling
   Child labour is harmful and illegal.

22. A — Day of the African Child
   16 June is the Day of the African Child.

23. A — 18 years
   The law says a person must be 18 to marry.

24. B — Everyone has a voice
   Democracy makes everyone heard.

25. D — A village elder
   A village elder knows leadership.

26. B — Chief
   A chief leads a location.

27. C — Defence and security
   Defence is national.

28. D — The county assembly
   The assembly must approve them.

29. D — The deputy governor
   The deputy governor supports the governor.

30. D — Sharing power and resources between the national and county governments
   Devolution moves some power to counties.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Harambee is people pulling together to solve a problem, for example to build a school or a clinic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

32. (5 marks)
   Answer: Visitors pay park and hotel fees. Guides and drivers get jobs. Hotels and shops earn money. Local crafts are sold. The county earns taxes to build roads and clinics.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: The county assembly is the group of elected members (MCAs) that makes laws for the county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for group of MCAs, 1 mark for making county laws.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: A compass is used to find direction. Its needle points to north.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for finding direction, 1 mark for the needle pointing north.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty helps us to be trusted. Respect keeps peace. Responsibility helps us to do our duties. Accept other valid values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each value with a reason.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Announce, nominate candidates, campaign, vote, count votes in public, and declare the winner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each group of two correct steps.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep customs, settle disputes and advise at ceremonies.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.

38. (5 marks)
   Answer: It helps us to find our way. It helps mapmakers to draw maps. It helps us to describe where places are. It helps drivers and sailors to travel. It helps us to plan journeys.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 5.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Write a polite invitation, state the topic, give the date and time, and thank the visitor after the talk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sugar factory uses sugarcane, tea factory uses tea leaves, cement factory uses limestone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each industry with its material.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Opening, reading the last minutes, reports from cabinet members, suggestions from classes, and closing remarks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: It means sharing power and resources between the national government and county governments.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing power, 1 mark for national and county.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Project manager leads the team, treasurer keeps money records, production team makes the goods, sales team sells the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role and duty pair.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10,000 more people.
   Working / marking points: 12 x 1,000 = 12,000; 2 x 1,000 = 2,000; 12,000 - 2,000 = 10,000. 1 mark for each step.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: They have the same rights as other children. They may be laughed at or neglected. Including them helps them to learn and be happy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
